architecture.title: 1. System Architecture
architecture.li13: Google sign-in (OpenID Connect, turned on by environment variables)

env.title: 3. Environment Variables
env.secretKeyDesc: JWT signing key. Must be set in production
env.envDesc: Environment mode. Error if SECRET_KEY is not set in production
env.dbDesc: PostgreSQL URL. Local example: postgresql+psycopg2://ymtc:ymtc@127.0.0.1:54329/ymtc. In deployment, the Supabase transaction pooler
env.tokenDesc: Session length for a normal login (hours)
env.warn1: Warning: In production, you must set SECRET_KEY to a unique value. The server will fail to start if not set.
env.dbDirectDesc: Direct (or session pooler) URL used only for migrations. Falls back to DATABASE_URL when empty
env.storageDesc: Storage for attachments and import files. local or supabase (deployment)
env.supabaseDesc: Supabase project URL, service key, bucket name. Used when STORAGE_BACKEND=supabase
env.cronDesc: Secret for the daily maintenance job (/api/internal/cron/daily)
env.proxyDesc: Proxy header that carries the client IP. Use only a header your hosting platform overwrites (Vercel: x-real-ip)
env.rememberDesc: Session length in days when "Remember me" is checked
env.lockDesc: Maximum wait for the concurrent edit lock (milliseconds). Beyond it, the request gets a 409 notice
env.googleDesc: OAuth client for Google sign-in. Leave empty to hide the Google button
env.googleRedirectDesc: Redirect URI registered in the Google console. Required in production (ENV=production)
env.companyDomainsDesc: Company Google Workspace domains (comma separated). An account counts as a company account only by the Workspace domain Google reports
env.allowPersonalDesc: 0 accepts company accounts only. AUTH_COMPANY_DOMAINS must be set, and email sign-ups always wait for approval
env.approvalDesc: Who needs administrator approval. none (nobody) / personal (only company Workspace Google accounts skip approval; email sign-ups wait even with a company address) / all (everyone). With AUTH_ALLOW_PERSONAL=0, email sign-ups always wait for approval regardless of this value
env.bootstrapDesc: Value required to create the first administrator on an empty production database (ENV=production)
env.registerLimitDesc: Sign-up requests allowed per IP per hour
env.googleSetupOl1: In the Google Cloud console, go to APIs & Services > Credentials and create an OAuth client ID (Web application).
env.googleSetupOl2: Add https://<site address>/api/auth/google/callback to Authorized redirect URIs. For development, use http://localhost:5173/api/auth/google/callback.
env.googleSetupOl3: Put the issued values in GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, put the same redirect URI in GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI, and restart the server. The login screen then shows Sign in with Google.
env.googleSetupInfo: Company accounts only: put your Workspace domain in AUTH_COMPANY_DOMAINS and set AUTH_ALLOW_PERSONAL=0. AUTH_APPROVAL decides who waits for approval (in company-only mode, email sign-ups always wait). If a value is invalid, the server stops at startup and tells you why.

database.title: 4. Database
database.li1: PostgreSQL 17. Locally, start it from the repo root with docker compose up -d --wait db (127.0.0.1:54329)
database.li2: Alembic migrations create the schema. The local server runs alembic upgrade head on startup; in deployment the Deploy workflow runs it before deploying.
database.li3: Move SQLite data from v1.10.3.1 and earlier with scripts/migrate_sqlite_to_pg.py. The SQLite version remains on the sqlite-legacy branch.
database.testCasesRel: Belongs to project, supports soft delete
database.testPlansRel: Belongs to project, linked to test_runs (1:N)
database.apiKeysRel: Belongs to a user, all revoked when the password changes
database.softDeleteInfo: Test cases are soft-deleted (deleted_at field is set). They are permanently deleted after 7 days. Deleted TCs can be restored via the restore API (POST /api/projects/{id}/testcases/{tc_id}/restore).

userMgmt.title: 5. User Management
userMgmt.li1: Access the admin page by clicking the "Admin" button in the header.
userMgmt.li2: For each user you see the username, display name, email, sign-in method (password, Google, and the linked Google address), status, system role, project assignment, and join date.
userMgmt.ol1: Change the role dropdown for the target user.
userMgmt.ol3: New permissions apply from the user's next API call.
userMgmt.roleChangeWarn: Warning: If you revoke your own Admin role, you will lose access to the admin page. Always maintain at least one Admin.
userMgmt.resetOl1: Click the "Reset" button in the password column of the target user's row.
userMgmt.resetOl2: A 12-character temporary password is generated and displayed.
userMgmt.resetOl3: Share the temporary password with the user.
userMgmt.resetOl4: The user will see a forced password change screen on their next login.
userMgmt.resetPwWarn: Warning: The temporary password is displayed only once. Make sure to note it down before sharing.
userMgmt.resetApiKeyInfo: Note: Resetting a password also revokes all of that user's API keys. Password resets, approving or rejecting recovery requests and sign-ups, role changes, disabling or enabling, releasing an email and deleting an account can be done only from a signed-in admin session, not with an API key.
userMgmt.initialAccountInfo: When there are no users, the sign-up page becomes Create administrator account and that account is the Admin. In production you must also enter the BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN value. Later users sign up with email and start as User.
userMgmt.accountRequestP1: Requests for finding a username or resetting a password, submitted from the login screen's "Account Help" link, are processed on the admin page.
userMgmt.accountRequestImgAlt: Admin page - Account recovery request queue
userMgmt.accountRequestOl1: Check pending requests in the "Account Requests" list at the bottom of the admin page.
userMgmt.accountRequestOl2: Verify the requester's identity using the contact info and note.
userMgmt.accountRequestOl3: Select the target account from the dropdown and click Approve. If identity cannot be verified, click Reject and provide a reason.
userMgmt.accountRequestOl4: The approval result is displayed on screen. For find-username requests the username is shown; for password resets, a one-time code is shown.
userMgmt.accountRequestWarn: Warning: The code is stored on the server only as a hash, and the plaintext is displayed on this screen only once. Be sure to copy it with the copy button and deliver it to the user right away. Once you click Close, it cannot be viewed again.
userMgmt.accountStatusLi1: Accounts are Active / Pending approval / Disabled. AUTH_APPROVAL decides who waits for approval. In company-only mode (AUTH_ALLOW_PERSONAL=0), email sign-ups always wait for approval.
userMgmt.accountStatusLi2: Pending accounts appear above the list as N pending approval. Approve lets them sign in; Reject deletes the account.
userMgmt.accountStatusLi3: Disable blocks sign-in and API keys immediately. Enabling again does not revive old API keys. You cannot disable or demote yourself or the last active administrator.
userMgmt.accountStatusLi4: Release email removes an email from an account that claimed someone else's address. Emails verified by Google cannot be released.
userMgmt.accountStatusLi5: Delete removes only accounts with no activity at all. Use it to clean up accounts created by mistake. Accounts with activity are refused; disable them instead.
userMgmt.accountStatusLi6: The linked Google address appears under the sign-in column. address not recorded means the account was linked before this feature; it fills in at the next Google sign-in. An empty Google-only account (no password) is removed automatically when its owner links that Google account to another account, even if it is pending or disabled. The last active administrator is never removed this way. If that account has activity or a password, linking is refused; reset its password to unlink Google, then link again.
userMgmt.accountStatusWarn: Note: Deleting a Workspace account does not end app sessions (up to 30 days) or API keys. Disable the user to block them immediately.

roleSystem.title: 6. Roles & Permissions
roleSystem.adminPerms: All features + user management + password reset + role change
roleSystem.qaPerms: User list view + access to all projects
roleSystem.projAdminDesc: Project management, TC CRUD, run management, member management, settings
roleSystem.projTesterDesc: Test execution, result recording, attachment upload
roleSystem.projLi1: Private projects are accessible only to members or the creator.
roleSystem.projLi2: Public projects are viewable by all authenticated users, but editing depends on project role.
roleSystem.projLi3: System Admin / QA Manager can access all projects.
roleSystem.pwReuseVal: Not allowed (rejected if same as current password)
roleSystem.pwForceChangeVal: Forced on next login after admin reset

projectMgmt.title: 7. Project Operations
projectMgmt.deleteWarn: When a project is deleted, the following data is permanently deleted:
projectMgmt.jiraLi1: Set the issue tracker URL in project settings. Jira and Linear are supported.
projectMgmt.jiraLi2: Example: https://your-domain.atlassian.net (Jira), https://linear.app/your-workspace (Linear). For other tools, include a {key} placeholder, e.g. https://tracker.example.com/items/{key}.
projectMgmt.jiraLi3: Issue keys (e.g., PROJ-123) in a test result's Issue Link open the matching issue from the ↗ in the test run sheet and from the report.

fileMgmt.title: 8. File / Attachment Management
fileMgmt.storagePathVal: Local: UPLOAD_DIR (default: backend/uploads). Deployment: private Supabase Storage bucket (STORAGE_BACKEND=supabase)
fileMgmt.downloadSecVal: Unsafe MIME types forced to octet-stream download
fileMgmt.tip1: Disk management: When a test run is deleted, related attachment files are also automatically deleted (based on UPLOAD_DIR). Check disk usage periodically.

security.title: 9. Security Settings
security.pwResetImpl: Admin issues temporary password, forced change
security.authTokenSetting: TOKEN_EXPIRE_HOURS (default 72 hours); Remember me uses REMEMBER_ME_DAYS (default 30 days)
security.apiKeyImpl: Per-user create · revoke, SHA-256 hash stored, Bearer header auth
security.apiKeySetting: Expiry 30 · 90 · 180 · 365 days or never, 20 per user, all revoked when the password changes
security.csrfSetting: Auto-applied on state-changing requests from cookie sessions (Bearer header auth excluded)
security.loginLimitSetting: 10 attempts per IP+user in 5 min (locked on exceed)
security.googleImpl: OpenID Connect authorization code flow + PKCE, state and nonce checks, only emails verified by Google
security.signupImpl: Per-IP sign-up rate limit, administrator approval

apiRef.title: 10. Main API Endpoints
apiRef.swaggerInfo: Only frequently used endpoints are listed. For the full list and request formats, see Swagger UI at

auth.title: Auth
auth.checkUsername: Check username availability. First-admin screen only; 404 once any user exists
auth.config: Login screen settings (whether the Google button shows, which sign-up screen)
auth.register: Sign up with email; may wait for approval. Also creates the first administrator
auth.login: Login (issues a session cookie; 30 days by default with remember_me)
auth.logout: Logout. Clears the session cookie and ends that account's sessions on other devices too (signed-in session only)
auth.changePassword: Change password. 8 chars to 72 bytes (signed-in session only)
auth.approveUser: Approve a sign-up (Admin, signed-in session only)
auth.rejectUser: Reject a sign-up; deletes the pending account (Admin, signed-in session only)
auth.disableUser: Disable; blocks login and API keys (Admin, signed-in session only)
auth.releaseEmail: Release the email (Admin, signed-in session only)
auth.deleteUser: Delete an account with no work history; 409 if it has history (Admin, signed-in session only)
auth.approveAccountRequest: Approve account recovery request (Admin, signed-in session only)
auth.rejectAccountRequest: Reject account recovery request (Admin, signed-in session only)
auth.listApiKeys: List own API keys (signed-in session only)
auth.createApiKey: Create an API key; the raw key is returned once (signed-in session only)
auth.revokeApiKey: Revoke an API key (signed-in session only)
auth.googleCallback: Google sign-in callback; the address GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI points to
auth.googleUnlink: Unlink Google (accounts with a password only)

testRuns.title: Test Runs
testRuns.importResults: Import automation result file (Playwright JSON · JUnit XML, ?dry_run · keep_executed · label)
testRuns.importByName: Upload a result file by run name; creates the next round of that name (?run_name · round=next|open · version · environment · sheet_names · dry_run)
testRuns.clone: Clone run. ?next_round=true creates the next round of the same name (max round + 1, plan inherited)

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.stability: TC stability: result changes across rounds and always failing TCs (?version · date_from · date_to · min_runs · limit)

runIssues.title: Run issues (report issue section)
runIssues.create: Add issue (title · url required; issue_key · status · note · tc_ids · origin_run_id · verdict). Same url is 409
runIssues.update: Update issue (verdict: resolved · open · partial · unverified)
runIssues.carryOver: Carry over previous issues (body from_run_id, defaults to the comparison target; same url skipped)

troubleshoot.title: 11. Troubleshooting
troubleshoot.r4c: Frontend origin not in allowed list
troubleshoot.r4f: Add origin to CORS_ORIGINS env variable
troubleshoot.r5c: File size exceeded or disallowed extension
troubleshoot.r5f: Check file is under 50MB with allowed extension
troubleshoot.r6f: Re-save file as UTF-8, verify after build
troubleshoot.r7c: Header mapping failed or invalid file format
troubleshoot.r7f: Check supported formats (.xlsx, .csv, .md) and the header row. Save legacy .xls files as .xlsx in Excel. CSV auto-detects UTF-8/CP949
troubleshoot.r8f: Create custom-fields via API then refresh
troubleshoot.r9s: Every API returns 503 (DB schema older than the code)
troubleshoot.r9c: New code pulled without running the DB migration
troubleshoot.r9f: Run python -m alembic upgrade head in backend. In deployment the Deploy workflow does it
troubleshoot.r10f: Ensure test_plan_id is set when creating Run
troubleshoot.r11c: No usable Korean font (the Pretendard files in backend/fonts are missing from the deployment, and the server has neither Malgun Gothic nor NanumGothic)
troubleshoot.r11f: Include backend/fonts/Pretendard-*.ttf in the deployment. Check the server log for "한글 폰트를 찾을 수 없습니다"
troubleshoot.r12s: "Another operation is in progress" when saving
troubleshoot.r12c: Concurrent sheet or test case structure changes in the same project waited too long for a lock
troubleshoot.r12f: Retry shortly. If it happens often, raise LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS (default 10000)
troubleshoot.r13s: No Google button on the login screen
troubleshoot.r13f: Set the GOOGLE_* values as in 3-1 and restart the server
troubleshoot.r14s: redirect_uri_mismatch error on the Google screen
troubleshoot.r14c: The redirect URI registered in the Google console differs from GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI
troubleshoot.r14f: Make the two values identical, including a trailing / and http vs https
troubleshoot.r15s: Login fails with "waiting for administrator approval"
troubleshoot.r15c: The account is pending under AUTH_APPROVAL, or it is an email sign-up in company-only mode
troubleshoot.r15f: Approve the account in User Management (5-4-1)

backup.title: 12. Backup & Recovery
backup.tip1: Deployment: the Backup workflow in the private repo keeps a daily DB dump (public schema) and the Storage objects as artifacts (14 days). Supabase DB backups do not include Storage objects, so keep both.
